transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
After Democrats won full control of Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections,
California Congressman Robert Garcia is set to become the next chair of the House Oversight Committee.
And he's promising to look into funding for President Trump's immigration enforcement operations.
Here's NPR's Jasmine Garst.
The current Congress basically gave immigration enforcement a blank check.
In 2025 and 2026, Congress gave around $240 billion,
that's billion with a B, to ICE and Customs and Border Patrol.
Now, the incoming Congress, which just got voted in, could stop giving them even more money.
But, you know, the truth is ICE and DHS have gotten enough funds to run mass deportation operations for the remainder of Trump's term.
Colorado's 5th congressional district has flipped and elected its first ever Democratic Representative Brianna Heaney of Member Station KRCC has more.
Jessica Killen will become the district's first Democratic Congressperson in its nearly 60-year history.
Colorado Springs is the heart of the district.
It's long been known as one of the top conservative cities in the country.
Incumbent Jeff Crank won the district by 14 points two years ago.
Killen says it's not about the blue wave, but instead a return to normalcy.
It's not that people are loving Democrats right now, they're just not happy with what's happening.
So I am more focused on the work ahead and what we have to do to deliver results.
Killen is a veteran and previously worked for the Biden administration.
She won by nearly five points.
For NPR News, I'm Brianna Heaney in Colorado Springs.
The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services must restart certifying 19,000 new health insurance brokers Friday.
That's according to a federal court order.
The agency had halted all certification of new brokers as part of a fraud crackdown.
Alex Olgin reports.
In September, CMS unexpectedly froze all new broker licenses and ended 760,000 people's health plans.
The agency claimed this was to fight fraudulent enrollments which have landed a few brokers in prison.
The moratorium caused chaos for brokers prepping for the November open enrollment period.
Johnny Wallen with Health Insurance Exchange Group is trying to rehire people.
I immediately started calling and messaging some of the people that we had that we ended up having to let go
because they're not being able to pay the license to help.
Democratic senators are now probing insurers.
They say plan cancellations are only possible because insurers were quietly colluding with the Trump administration.
For NPR News, I'm Alex Olgin.
A selloff of stocks linked to artificial intelligence is ongoing.
Asian shares tumbling with South Korean stocks leading to climbers.
South Korean shares down more than 6 percent, followed closely by shares in Japan.
This is NPR News.
A Florida sheriff says a government who killed a woman before being fatally shot by a security guard at Citibank's office complex in Tampa
targeted the campus because he was angry over a $2,500 debt collection.
Hillsborough County Sheriff Chad Chronister says a man called an attorney affiliated with Citibank hours before Wednesday's shooting
and threatened violence of a court hearing over the debt was not canceled.
A British man in the Democratic Republic of Congo has tested positive for Ebola.
NPR's Jonathan Lambert reports on the first case of Ebola for a British national since the outbreak began in May.
The U.K. government confirmed that the man will be flown back home for treatment.
It's unclear how he got the disease, though Reuters reports that he was in DRC as a health care worker.
Officials say the U.K. has well-established procedures for dealing with diseases like this and that the risk to the general public is low.
This is the fifth Ebola case ever treated in the country.
The infection comes as the virus continues spreading across DRC.
More than 10,000 people have been infected and at least 5,100 have died.
There are no approved vaccines or treatments for the kind of Ebola behind this outbreak.
While the mortality rate is high where the virus is spreading, patients treated in higher income countries tend to recover.
Jonathan Lambert, NPR News.
One of the outstanding races left over from Tuesday's midterm elections has been decided.
Los Angeles getting a new mayor, City Council member Neetha Rahman has defeated incumbent mayor Karen Bass.
Rahman is a Democratic socialist.
I'm Jael Snyder. This is NPR News.

Colorado's 5th district elects Democrat Jessica Killen, its first Democratic representative in nearly 60 years
CMS ordered to resume certifying 19,000 health insurance brokers after fraud-crackdown freeze
Asian stock markets tumble in selloff of AI-linked shares, South Korean shares down over 6 percent
